findings.title: A TAC with the strongest keyword is stored readable when its digits are grouped with commas: 'Your TAC is 482, 913', 'Your TAC is 4, 8, 2, 9, 1, 3', 'Your TAC is 48, 29, 13'
findings.detail:
The filter's code pattern groups digits only by a single space or hyphen. The mask joins digits across up to three non-letter characters, except that a comma or dot joins only when it stands alone (so 'No. 123, 9:47 PM' and 'RM12.90, 3 items' stay apart). A comma followed by a space therefore ends the run for the mask, and each group of 1-3 digits is too short to mask. Both lines of defence miss: the notification is kept, unmasked and with maybeOtp = false. Same class as run 6's finding 10 (fixed): a gap shape neither line reads. How likely: no bank is known to print these, but '4, 8, 2, 9, 1, 3' is how a screen reader or a voice message reads a code, and the gate also runs on any app chosen through *More*. D119's reason for masking everything is the shape nobody predicted. Also readable: '482 , 913', '482 - - 913' (four separators), '482. 913', '482 / / 913', '482 ,913', '482,, 913'.

Suggested fix: count a comma, or a dot followed by a space, as a joiner between digits in the mask. Decimal amounts are already carved out per token ('12.90' stays), so 'RM12.90, 3 items' still keeps its amount and its 3. Add the shapes to OtpMaskTest and OtpFilterTest.
findings.repro: gradle -p apps/shell/core jar && gradle -p qa/B02/core-probe test --tests 'Probe7.after_strong_keyword_odd_gaps'

findings.title: No test checks that CaptureGate stores the title and the expanded text masked: storing either as posted leaves all 43 core tests green
findings.detail:
OtpMaskTest calls `OtpMask.apply` directly, including on three parts at once, but nothing asserts what the gate stores. The gate takes `masked.parts` and builds the RawEvent from it. If that line reads `p.title` or `p.bigText`, a code in the title or the expanded text is stored raw and the key is hashed from it: the whole of D119 gone for two of three fields. The emulator tests post only a title and a text, and assert on `text`. Banks put codes in the expanded text (BigTextStyle) as readily as in the text. Probe7's test goes red for all three fields; the suite does for the text field only.

Suggested fix: a CaptureGateTest that keeps a notification with a number in each of title, text and expanded text and asserts none is left in any field.
findings.repro: In apps/shell/core/.../CaptureGate.kt change `val (title, text, bigText) = masked.parts` to `val (title, text) = masked.parts; val bigText = p.bigText`; gradle -p apps/shell/core test --rerun-tasks (green); git checkout -- the file. Same with `val (_, text, bigText) = masked.parts; val title = p.title`. Then gradle -p qa/B02/core-probe test --tests Probe7.after_gate_masks_every_stored_field (red).
findings.evidence:
expanded text as posted: BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 43 tests, 0 failed
title as posted:         BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 43 tests, 0 failed
text as posted:          43 tests completed, 7 failed
Probe7.after_gate_masks_every_stored_field: FAILED for each of the three

findings.title: Captured on this phone collapses line breaks and repeated spaces in the expanded text, though it says 'as the apps wrote them'
findings.detail: The rows are plain paragraphs (white-space: normal). Android's expanded text for an inbox-style notification is the lines joined with a newline (Capture.read), and Share samples keeps those newlines, so the soak owner sees one thing on screen and pastes another. A stored 'Line one / Line two / (blank) / Line four   spaced' shows as 'Line one Line two Line four spaced'. The numbers are masked correctly; this is only layout. Suggested: `whitespace-pre-line` (or pre-wrap) on the title, text and expanded text paragraphs.
findings.evidence: Error: expanded text with 4 lines and a blank line renders 1 line(s), white-space=normal   (R7 newline rendering {"h":20,"lh":20,"ws":"normal"})

findings.title: A group summary, an ongoing notification, a dropped channel or an empty one from a chosen app is dropped with no trace, though §6.2 and D115 say each drop from a chosen app is logged
findings.detail: D115: 'Each drop from a chosen app is logged by time and app, never text, so a dropped payment can be found'. `Capture.store` logs only `DropReason.OTP` and a gate failure ('unread'). A payment posted as an ongoing notification (D115 assumes none is) or inside a group summary would vanish with nothing in the heartbeat, and the soak is exactly where that assumption gets tested. Read from Capture.kt, not run on a device. Either log those drops by time and app too (no text), or amend D115 and §6.2 to say only OTP and unread drops are logged.
findings.evidence: if (d.reason == DropReason.OTP) Heartbeat.dropped(context, posted)   // the only drop reason that is logged

findings.title: Capture.store's insert is outside the try, so a SQLite failure on the capture thread is uncaught (read, not run)
findings.detail: `gate.decide` and `outbox.droppedChannels()` are guarded ('never crash the listener over one notification'), but `outbox.insert(d.event)` and the heartbeat writes run on `worker.execute { ... }` unguarded. An uncaught exception on that thread (disk full, a corrupt database) reaches Android's default handler and ends the process; the listener restarts, but the notification may already be gone from the tray's replay. Rare. Not run: no device.
findings.evidence: worker.execute { store(app, posted) }   // no catch around the insert

findings.title: The mask joins digits across any short non-letter gap (slash, colon, bullet, underscore), so dates and times lose digits §6.2 doesn't list
findings.detail: §6.2 and D119 list 'spaces, dashes, dots, brackets and invisible characters'. Since run 6 the mask joins across any non-letter character, so '12/9/2026' becomes '••/•/••••', '9:47:05 PM' becomes '•:••:•• PM' and 'Ref 12 34 56' becomes 'Ref •• •• ••'. That is the safe direction (D119 accepts over-masking), but §6.2 should say it, since the template drafter and the soak will meet it.
findings.evidence:
after_overmask: Paid on 12/9/2026 at 9:47:05 PM -> Paid on ••/•/•••• at •:••:•• PM
after_overmask: Posted 2026-10-09T21:47:05 -> Posted ••••-••-••T••:••:••

findings.title: The simulator keeps nothing across a reload and posts only six fixed notifications, so a browser walk proves the screen, never the mask or the offline outbox (carries run 6's finding 14)
findings.detail: After a reload the simulator's events, chosen apps and access are all gone (zustand, memory only; localStorage is empty). Its dedupe identity omits the notification key and isn't length-prefixed. The Kotlin core and the emulator are the only places the gate and the outbox are exercised. The criteria that need a device (R7-AC-7, 19, 22, 26) are 'unreachable' here for that reason.

findings.title: Two tests that can't fail for the reason they name: DedupeKeyTest 'counts bytes, not characters', CaptureGateTest 'a payment is kept raw'
findings.detail: 'counts bytes' compares 'é' precomposed with 'e' + U+0301, which differ by characters and by bytes alike, so a character-counting prefix would still pass. 'a payment is kept raw' asserts only the title and the key's length, though its text now holds a masked date. Neither hides a bug today. Suggested: pin a key for a multi-byte field against a known hash, and rename the second test.
findings.evidence: assertNotEquals(DedupeKey.of("p","k",1,"é","",null), DedupeKey.of("p","k",1,"é","",null))   // two different spellings of é

findings.title: By design, a number straight after a currency and any number with exactly two decimals are never masked, however long: 'Your pass is RM482913', 'Ref 48291375.99'
findings.detail: §6.2: 'a decimal amount, or the number after a currency, is left'. The carve-outs hold any length up to 24 digits ('USD 48291375' stays). No bank is known to word a code that way, and the filter would drop one that also carries a keyword and isn't read as an amount; recorded because it is the one place a code can sit unmasked by rule. Probe7.after_currency_whole_number, after_decimal_shaped_code.
